clue.text: Reliable furniture desired by every MP?

definitions.text: Reliable furniture desired by every MP?

parts.words: Reliable furniture desired by every MP?
parts.note: read literally, a dependable chair; in politics, a constituency no MP can easily lose, which every member would love to hold

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament all hankering after sturdy chairs for the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reliable' is SAFE and 'furniture' a SEAT, but the whole clue points to the parliamentary sense: a constituency with a big majority.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency held by a large majority is what every sitting member hopes to represent, so the phrase fits the political wish.

clue.text: Plants some wood for guns

definitions.meaning: garden flowers of the genus Matthiola, scented bedding plants
the wooden butt and handle parts of rifles

explanation.definitionFit: Scented garden flowers carry this name, as do the wooden butts of rifles.

clue.text: A battleground happening to be a sporting contest?

parts.note: a field is where a battle is fought, as in field of battle
an event is something that happens

explanation.surface: A war-zone incident that turns out to be a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic competitions like the javelin or long jump are a kind of sporting contest.

clue.text: Aspen trees turned out to be a cause of disbelief on board!

definitions.text: a cause of disbelief on board!

indicators.note: turned out signals that the letters of Aspen trees are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Sailors amazed when some aspen trees are delivered on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors' tales of a giant monster in the ocean are met with disbelief by those aboard ship.

clue.text: People who love to have a quarrel like this

definitions.text: People who love to have a quarrel like this

parts.words: People who love to have a quarrel like this
parts.note: lovers proverbially have small, petty squabbles

explanation.surface: Couples who seem to enjoy arguing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People who love' are lovers, not people who enjoy rows; a lovers' squabble is a minor one.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor squabble between sweethearts is the classic lovers' quarrel.

clue.text: Almost stops in mid-sentence!

parts.note: punctuation marks that make a brief pause, nearly a full stop, placed inside sentences

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps breaking off while speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: These punctuation marks signal a short pause, less than a full stop, within a sentence.

clue.text: Deliveries of cows!

parts.note: reads like milk rounds or farm drop-offs; means the young that cows give birth to

explanation.surface: A farmer receiving a shipment of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows deliver young, and their newborn offspring are young bovines.

clue.text: Large number of clues about the strength of the body!

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: about here means the letters of clues are moved around

explanation.surface: Many crossword clues on the subject of physical fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical power comes from the contractile tissue of the body, and the word also means brawn.

clue.text: A bright pink salmon used with it to produce this popular paste

definitions.text: A bright pink salmon used with it to produce this popular paste

parts.words: A bright pink salmon used with it to produce this popular paste
parts.note: the word names both a bright pink colour and a small crustacean, mixed with salmon in a familiar sandwich spread

explanation.surface: A recipe for a well-known sandwich paste.
explanation.walkthrough: Salmon and shrimp paste was a common British sandwich spread sold in small jars.
explanation.definitionFit: The small crustacean gives its name to a bright pink colour and is paired with salmon in a jarred spread.

clue.text: Famous player shot at work

definitions.meaning: a celebrated actor in the cinema
a screen actor is shot, in the sense of filmed by cameras, while doing the job

explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a gunshot; here it means captured by a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated screen actor is a famous performer, and is filmed (shot) on the job.

clue.text: Cancels shouts from the wings

definitions.meaning: cries heard from offstage, in the wings of a theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The wings are the theatre's side areas out of the audience's sight, so cries from there are calls made off stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a fixture is to scrap it, and cries from backstage are calls heard from off the stage.

clue.text: More than one craze in the Orient just dies away

indicators.note: in places the letter for the Orient inside the crazes

parts.note: fads are crazes, plural
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A craze from the East that soon fizzles out.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle or grow faint is to die away gradually.

clue.text: Took off sheepskin coat

parts.note: reads like undressing from a fleece jacket, but describes clipping the wool from a sheep

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging off a sheepskin jacket on coming indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping a sheep's fleece is removing the animal's natural woolly covering.

clue.text: Come forward to get increase

definitions.meaning: to volunteer or advance from a group
a rise, as in a raise in level

explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to advance from the ranks, and a rise in level is an upward move.

clue.text: Is it full of uniformed coachmen?

definitions.text: Is it full of uniformed coachmen?

parts.words: Is it full of uniformed coachmen?
parts.note: coachmen read as men in railway coaches; uniformed suggests soldiers travelling together

explanation.surface: A carriage crowded with liveried drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coachmen' suggests horse-drawn drivers; here it means men riding in railway coaches, and uniformed means they are soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway service carrying soldiers is packed with uniformed men riding in carriages.

clue.text: Create facade for stage show

definitions.meaning: to pretend or keep up a false front
to present a performance in a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: Pretending is keeping up a false front, and a performer mounts a theatre routine.

clue.text: Makes level the odds

definitions.meaning: betting odds of one to one, where the stake is matched

explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a one-to-one price is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: To equalise something is to make it flat or balanced, and one-to-one betting odds carry the same name.

clue.text: Blow to chastise head boy who's a ruffian

indicators.note: head means only the first letter of the word chastise is used

parts.note: a lout is a rough, uncouth youth

explanation.surface: A headmaster tempted to strike a delinquent pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy hit with the hand is a whack, and that is this word's everyday sense.

clue.text: Hold it inside

parts.note: reads as a request to keep something in; the hold is the lower part of a ship, where freight is carried

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep something hidden or suppressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is the goods stowed in a ship's hold.

clue.text: King to go back after tea break, seeing turn

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: go back tells us the little word to is written backwards
break means the letters of tea are smashed and reset in a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch returning to duties after a tea break, observing a change of shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back' turns TO into OT, and 'break' rearranges TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin round an axis is to revolve, which is a turn.

clue.text: Generally grey ferret is its enemy

definitions.text: Generally grey ferret is its enemy

parts.words: Generally grey ferret is its enemy
parts.note: a grey-furred animal hunted by ferrets in warrens

explanation.surface: A remark about the grey ferret and its foes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grey' looks like it describes the ferret; it describes the prey. Ferrets are traditionally used to drive this animal from burrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrets are sent into burrows to flush out this usually grey-brown burrowing mammal.

clue.text: Walked to get lamb turnover for top journalist

indicators.note: turnover signals the letters of lamb are turned about into a new order

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Strolling over to fetch a lamb pastry for the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnover is also a pastry, which gives the surface its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolled at a leisurely pace means walked.

clue.text: Has being six set everything awry?

indicators.note: everything awry says all the letters of six and set are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A question about whether six sets made a total mess of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive or real is to have being.

clue.text: Is sorry about present being broken

indicators.note: being broken signals that the letters of present are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone apologising after a gift got smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who feels contrition and regret for a wrong is sorry.

clue.text: Cut in the cavalry

parts.note: the curved swords of horse soldiers, and also the verb for slashing with them

explanation.surface: A reduction in cavalry numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a budget reduction; it is the slashing done with cavalry swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse soldiers carried curved swords, and to strike with one is to slash.

clue.text: Turned to one side to make an entrance

definitions.text: Turned to one side to make an entrance

parts.words: Turned to one side to make an entrance
parts.note: sounds like an actor stepping aside on stage, but describes the handle twisted to open a door

explanation.surface: A performer stepping sideways to come on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A round handle on a door is twisted round to let someone in.

clue.text: Beaten by soldiers not in the fighting

definitions.text: Beaten by soldiers not in the fighting

parts.words: Beaten by soldiers not in the fighting
parts.note: a percussion instrument struck by army musicians who march rather than fight

explanation.surface: Troops defeated without ever joining battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' suggests defeat; it means struck, as by a military bandsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument is struck by military bandsmen, who play rather than fight.

clue.text: Isn't a sportsman defeated?

parts.note: someone who sulks after being beaten shows no sportsmanship when defeated

explanation.surface: A question about whether every athlete eventually loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes defeat ungraciously is no good sport when beaten.

clue.text: Non-professional people working in these exchanges

definitions.meaning: skilled manual occupations such as plumbing, as opposed to the professions

explanation.definitionFit: Crafts like carpentry are skilled occupations distinct from the professions, and swaps are deals of barter.

clue.text: Mighty men alter name-tags

indicators.note: alter tells us to change the order of the letters in name-tags

explanation.surface: Powerful men changing their identity badges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tycoons of industry are wealthy, powerful people.
